architecture.mechanism: The battery housing acts as a dedicated safety/thermal barrier whose material system supplies fire resistance and thermal management, containing cell-level thermal runaway inside the pack rather than letting it propagate to the vehicle underbody.
architecture.intervention: Specify the R519 traction battery pack enclosure as a fire-rated housing (aluminum/steel or sandwich/hybrid multi-material design per the review) with thermal insulation and fire-resistant layers sized to contain a single-cell runaway event under normal driving conditions.
architecture.expected_effect: Thermal runaway initiated in one cell/module is contained by the housing's fire resistance and thermal management functions, preventing flame/hot-gas escape to the underbody and eliminating the underbody fire while the vehicle is moving at speed.
architecture.falsification_test: Run an abuse-induced single-cell thermal runaway propagation test on a fully charged pack at 65 mph-equivalent airflow/underbody condition; pass requires no external flame, no housing burn-through, and no ignition of surrounding vehicle structure for 30 minutes post-trigger; a control pack without the fire-rated housing must show propagation (demonstrating the mechanism, not the test).
